subject: Prepay options & international invoicing: multi-year proposal for Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@acme.de>, Tomasz Nowak <tomasz.nowak@acme.de>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 09:47:00 +0100
Subject: Redwood multi-year prepay proposal + invoicing options

Hi Anna and Tomasz,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — good alignment on anticipated usage and the ramp profile for 2026. Per our discussion, attached is a clean copy of the multi-year prepay proposal (3-year, annual prepay with tiered term discounts) plus a sample PO template. High level:  

- Year 1 (prepay): 500k tokens/month baseline, billed annually up front
- Year 2: 1.0M tokens/month baseline (ramp), annual prepay with 7% term discount
- Year 3: 1.5M tokens/month baseline, annual prepay with 10% term discount

We intentionally separated the "term" discount (applied for committing to annual prepay each year) from the multi-year discount (applied on total committed value at signature). That gives flexibility if you want to annualize but keep the option to adjust baselines at each renewal. 

A few questions for your finance/legal so we can finalize: 
1) Which invoicing entity does Acme prefer? Redwood EU (Redwood Inference GmbH) or Redwood US (Redwood Inference, Inc.)? This affects VAT treatment.
2) Will Acme require invoices in EUR and payment in EUR (we can provide EUR invoices but our accounting will net FX differently)?
3) Any withholding tax (WHT) considerations we should account for in the SOW? If so, can you share the expected rates and whether Acme will provide a certificate to apply treaty relief?

If helpful, I can loop in our legal and tax folks to propose language (gross-up vs net) in the order form. Rishi and I are around all week for a quick call to run through the options.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

Attachments: RDW_Acme_MultiYear_Pricing_Proposal_20251105.pdf, Acme_PO_template.pdf

From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@acme.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tomasz Nowak <tomasz.nowak@acme.de>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 11:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood multi-year prepay proposal + invoicing options

Hi Marissa — thanks, proposal received. A few items from procurement/finance: 

- Acme prefers to be invoiced by Redwood Inference GmbH (EU entity) if available — simplifies VAT (reverse charge may apply).
- We prefer EUR invoicing and payment. Can you confirm if Redwood will accept EUR bank transfers for the annual prepay?
- Withholding tax: for services paid to non-EU entities we sometimes have to apply WHT, but if invoiced by the EU entity this should not be necessary. I will confirm with tax.

One more ask: can you provide an option that keeps Year 1 as an "annual prepay with monthly usage reconciliation" rather than a hard baseline? Means we prepay a pool and you invoice/credit any major overages/underages at year-end. That helps our cash planning.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Müller
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
anna.mueller@acme.de

Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 13:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood multi-year prepay proposal + invoicing options

Thanks Anna — good notes. Quick replies below and a couple of follow ups: 

1) EU invoicing: yes, Redwood Inference GmbH can issue invoices in EUR. That will generally make VAT handling simpler and avoid WHT on service fees in most jurisdictions. Our finance team can supply EUR bank details and IBAN.

2) EUR payment: accepted. We will show prices in EUR on the order form and can accept a single EUR transfer for the annual prepay. Please note: where contract lists USD list price with EUR invoicing, we apply FX conversion on the invoice date. If you prefer fixed EUR amounts, we can create a EUR-denominated order form to eliminate FX variance.

3) Withholding tax: if invoiced by the EU entity and services are rendered to Acme Germany, WHT is typically not applicable. If Acme must withhold, Redwood requests a tax certificate so we can gross-up or apply an offset. Olga, can you advise on recommended contract language (gross-up vs netting) and whether we should require certificate at PO stage?

4) Year 1 reconciliation: we can offer an annual reconciliation model (prepay pool with billed true-up). The trade-off is slightly smaller term discount in Year 1 (we would move Year 1 term discount from 5% to 3% if you take reconciliation). I have updated the attached with a reconciliation line item — see page 3.

Proposed next steps: 
- Anna/Tomasz confirm preferred invoicing entity and whether you want a EUR-denominated order form.
- If WHT may apply, Acme to share expected WHT rate and whether treaty relief docs will be provided.
- If ok, we prepare a draft OF + annex with the reconciliation approach for signature (and DocuSign). 

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to finalize.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: RDW_Acme_MultiYear_Pricing_Proposal_20251105.pdf (updated)

From: Tomasz Nowak <tomasz.nowak@acme.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Anna Müller <anna.mueller@acme.de>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 09:36:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood multi-year prepay proposal + invoicing options

Marissa — quick tax follow-up from our side: 

- We expect that if invoiced by Redwood GmbH there will be no WHT for services. That said, Acme sometimes needs to apply 15% withholding for certain cross-border vendors until treaty paperwork is provided. Can Redwood accept a clause that allows for gross-up OR that we deduct WHT and Acme issues a tax certificate to claim the credit? Finance prefers the latter (deduction + certificate) to avoid immediate cash outflows. 

- FX: if you generate EUR invoices but Redwood accounts in USD internally, will Acme be exposed to any reconciliation charges? We prefer fixed EUR amounts on the order form so our POs match invoices exactly.

If you can provide suggested contract wording for the WHT handling and an example EUR-denominated order form, we can circulate to tax and sign quickly.

Thanks,
Tomasz
Senior Manager, Group Treasury — Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@acme.de>, Tomasz Nowak <tomasz.nowak@acme.de>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood multi-year prepay proposal + invoicing options

Hi Anna / Tomasz — looping in legal/tax as promised. Quick summary and proposed contract language options below. Please treat these as starting points; Olga will advise final wording for the order form annex. 

Option A (EU invoicing, no gross-up) — preferred by Acme finance: 
- Redwood Inference GmbH will issue EUR-denominated invoices. 
- Acme may deduct withholding tax where legally required; Acme will provide a valid tax certificate within 60 days. 
- Parties agree to cooperate in good faith to obtain treaty relief; Redwood will credit/deduct any amounts reimbursed after receipt of certificate. 

Option B (Gross-up) — Redwood preference when WHT is material: 
- If Acme is required by law to withhold, Acme will remit the net amount and Redwood will invoice the gross amount. Acme will provide tax documentation; where withholding applied, Redwood will issue a credit or adjust future invoicing to reflect treaty relief. 

FX handling: we can do a EUR-denominated order form (fixed EUR amounts). That will be the invoice amount and match your PO. Our accounting will record in USD for internal reporting — that will not change the amount payable by Acme. 

Reconciliation model for Year 1 (as requested): 
- Acme prepays an agreed pool (EUR X). Actual consumption is reconciled at contract year-end. Overages >10% billed pro rata; underutilization credited to Acme at the agreed token rate. Term discounts in Year 1 reduced by 2 percentage points for reconciliation option. 

Next steps I propose: 
1) Anna/Tomasz confirm Option A or B (or propose hybrid).
2) Olga will draft the short tax/WHT clause and a EUR OF template.
3) Marissa to issue DocuSign once language agreed.

Olga — can you draft the clause (two-paragraph) and attach the sample EUR order form? Marissa, I attached the updated proposal with the reconciliation line items and the PO template.

Thanks — Rishi
VP, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
